newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland discovers oil and gas deposits.
newsitem.headline: Poland discovers oil and gas deposits.

text.p: Poland has discovered oil and gas deposits near the northwestern town of Debno Lubuskie which are twice as big as all Polish oil reserves exploited so far, an official from the Polish Oil and Gas Mining Company said.
The Gazeta Wyborcza quoted Stanislaw Radecki of Polskie
Gornictwo Naftowe i Gazownictwo SA as saying the deposits would allow for an increase in domestic crude production to one million tonnes a year from the current 600,000 tonnes.
"It is the biggest oil deposit discovered in Poland. In five to six years we may raise domestic crude oil production even to one million tons annually," Radecki said.

The field is estimated by experts to contain 64.4 million tonnes of oil and 29.4 billion cubic metres of natural gas, of which some 10 million tonnes of oil and 10 billion cubic metres of gas can be recovered.
Currently exploited Polish oil deposits amount to 5.4 million tonnes, while usable gas deposits are estimated at 150 billion cubic metres.

The discovery will not significantly alter the amount of crude Poland has to import as the country imports some 90 percent of its oil. Seven Polish refineries process some 15 million tons of crude annually.
The new deposits have been investigated since 1989 at a cost of some $60 million so far.
